PRE-IMPLEMENTATION UI/UX PACKAGE · BATCHES 1–8 OF 8 · NOT ACCEPTED, NOT LOCKED

Bakchodi in Bali, with more than one of you in it.

Foundations, components, authentication and onboarding for the multi-user and Group evolution of the existing application. Every value on these boards is either lifted from src/styles/global.css and current component source, or explicitly labelled as an extension, a correction, or deferred.

Boards 01–24 Batches 7 and 8 add boards 18 and 20 · realtime and migration Ready for formal design acceptance review
BOARD 01

Visual source-of-truth summary

AUTHORITY 1 — CURRENT APPLICATION

Five-tab shell: Trip, Scan, Split, FX, Todo. Title Bakchodi in Bali, mono date line MAY 22 — 27 · 2026. Sticky translucent header carrying the current identity chip and the five-person chip rail. 480px cap at every viewport.

AUTHORITY 2 — BASELINE DOC

Token inventory, spacing rhythm, typography variation settings and state matrices are taken from the accepted baseline audit at commit b77d0f6, cross-checked against source.

AUTHORITY 5 — LEGACY ONLY

Six-tab nav with AI, the “Bali Bachelor Trip (v2 Demo)” title, three-person participant data and the legacy Group Settings screen are historical evidence. None of them is reused as a pattern here.

RECORDED CONFLICTS · CARRIED FORWARD, NOT SILENTLY RESOLVED

C-01 Navigation. Legacy captures show six tabs including AI; current source renders five. Multi-user work adds no sixth tab — Group management enters from the header, not the nav.

C-02 Group Settings. Legacy Group Settings has no current route. Board 16 will design it fresh from architecture, not from that capture.

C-03 Identity model. Current identity is a persona chosen from a fixed list of five, held in localStorage. Accounts, Groups and claimed participants replace that, so the persona picker becomes the participant-claim flow rather than a sign-in.

C-04 Design system — closed. The attached green enterprise-learning system contradicts authority 1 and is ignored entirely, as confirmed. Nothing in this package derives from it.

Rule P-01: the colour identifies a participant, not their role, permission or connection state. Avatar fill stays colour + '22', border colour + '66', exactly as Avatar.tsx does today.

Extension P-02: a Group can hold more than five participants. Beyond the five source hues, participants receive a warm neutral avatar — #C8B8A6 fill at 22 — rather than an invented sixth neon. Colour is never the only way to tell two people apart: initial, name and emoji always accompany it.

SEMANTIC · EXTENDED FROM EXISTING VALUES
Error · #FF2D78Already the Scan parse-error and expense-validation colour. Reused, not replaced.
Success · #00FFD1Already the “amounts match” colour in Add expense. Always paired with a ✓ glyph.
Caution · #FFD600Parse warnings, stale data, pending invitations. Always paired with a word.
Quiet · border-strongReconnecting, offline, read-only. Deliberately colourless so it stays calm.

DEFERRED

D-01 REMOTE IMAGERY
Hero and persona art is remote Supabase Storage with empty alt, and breaks in live captures. Boards here use a bordered warm placeholder plus a fallback rule; the delivery fix itself is an architecture decision, not a token.

D-02 NOTIFICATION SURFACE
Whether realtime events need a persistent surface, or only the inline treatments on board 17, stays open until architecture confirms the event volume.

D-03 EMOJI AS IDENTITY
Animal emoji are seeded per persona. Whether a new member picks an emoji, gets one assigned, or uses initials only is unresolved; boards fall back to the initial avatar.

Correction A-03: the Scan assignment toggle currently has no label association. Every toggle here has a visible label, a helper line stating what “off” means, and a 44px row.

VALIDATION TIMING · FORM-LEVEL FEEDBACK
ON BLURFormat checks — email shape, Group name length, password rules. Never while typing the first time.
ON CHANGE, AFTER FIRST ERROROnce a field has shown an error it re-validates as the user types, so the error clears the moment it is fixed.
ON SUBMITRequired-field checks, matching Amounts, and everything the server owns. Matches the current dialog behaviour.
We couldn't save thatTwo fields need attention. They're marked below.
✓Saved. Everyone in the Group sees it now.

Correction A-04: each error is programmatically tied to its input and announced politely; the form-level summary moves focus to the first offending field.

BOARD 07

Feedback, errors and permissions

Reusable blocks referenced by every later board. Permission copy says what the person can do next; it never names a policy, a table or a rule.

LOADING · SKELETON · IN-PROGRESS
Checking your invitation…

Three pulsing rows is the existing Trip skeleton. Reused verbatim for member lists, documents and settlements. Screen readers get a polite “loading” status; reduced motion drops the pulse.

EMPTY STATES · PLAYFUL IS ALLOWED HERE
No Groups yet.Start one for your trip, or paste an invitation someone sent you.
Just you so far.Invite the crew and the itinerary stops being a solo project.

Fraunces line, Inter line, one action. Same rhythm as “Nothing here yet.” and “All settled up.” in the current app.

CONNECTION · QUIET BY DESIGN
Reconnecting…
OFFLINEShowing what we last loaded.
✓Back in sync.
Astitva changed this expense while you had it open
Your edits are still here. Reload to see theirs.Reload

Connection states sit as a pill directly under the sticky header, inside the column. They never cover content and never animate in from the edge.

PERMISSION AND ACCESS · PLAIN LANGUAGE ONLY
This Group is archivedEverything is here to read. An Owner can restore it to start adding again.
Only an Owner can do thatInviting, removing and ownership changes stay with Owners. Partha and Astitva are Owners here.
That document is privateWhoever uploaded it kept it to themselves. Ask them to share it with the Group.
This Group isn't available to youYou may have been removed, or the link belongs to another account. Pick a Group you're in.

No status codes, no policy names, no “insufficient privileges”. Each block states the limit, then the next move. Where a person can help, they are named.

BOARD 14 · BATCH 3 · FLOW G · MOBILE 393 × 852

Permission, access and read-only states

Twenty screens. Two roles exist — Owner and Member — and read-only is a state of the Group, the session or the moment, never a third role. The backend stays deny-by-default; nothing here implies that a hidden or disabled control is the security. No policy name, table, status code or resource id appears in any string, and no screen reveals whether something a user cannot reach exists at all.

KNOWN AT RENDER TIME versus STALE DURING ACTION
Known at render timeNo enabled action the server would refuse. Owner-only configuration stays visible but closed, with one explanation. Irrelevant or dangerous actions are absent rather than dimmed. Nobody is allowed to fill in a form that cannot be submitted. PERM-05, 06, 07, 08, 10, 11, 12, 14
Stale or changed during the actionThe write reaches the server and fails there. Unsaved input is preserved locally and copyable, the screen states that nothing changed, the authorised view refreshes, and no success is shown before confirmation. PERM-13, 17, 18

BOARD 14 · FLOW E/G · CMP-20 · STATE: STALE-ROLE · SERVER-CONFIRMED
Session expired is not permission deniedThe two are told apart before anything renders, because confusing them is how an app ends up asking a signed-in person to sign in again.
SESSION EXPIRED“Signed out. Sign in to pick up where you left off.”Routes to authentication with a safe continuation, then returns to the same screen. The account is unknown, so no Group name and no trip data appear.AUTH-08 · CONTINUATION PRESERVED
PERMISSION DENIED“This trip isn’t available to you.”The session stays valid. The user keeps their account, their other trips and their place in the app. Never offers Sign in again.PERM-01 … PERM-18 · SESSION UNTOUCHED
If both are true — expired session and no membership — authentication wins, because the second answer isn’t knowable until someone is signed in.
PERM-19Session expired versus permission denied

The contract that keeps the two failure families apart. Expiry is an authentication event and routes to AUTH-08 with a continuation; denial is an authorisation outcome and leaves the session alone. No permission screen in this package contains a sign-in control.

How privacy is expressed: by absence. A stale reference gets one neutral sentence with no metadata; a private Event or document is simply not in the list and not in the count.

The permitted next action as one primary and at most one secondary. The eighth variant is the honest one: no action, and a sentence explaining why retrying cannot help.

BOARD 15 · BATCH 4 · FLOW H · MOBILE 393 × 852

Finance and settlement

Forty-seven screens on the existing Split tab. BalanceHero, GroupTotals, ExpenseCard, the Add and Edit dialogs and the Settle Up modal are reused as they are; what is added is multi-user truth — two independent exact-total checks, recorder attribution beside payer identity, inactive and unclaimed participants that stay attributable, a recorded accounting rate that live FX never rewrites, and a Group switch that clears one ledger before it draws another. Every figure on this board is the accepted arithmetic of the seeded trip at the recorded rate 188.68; anything that cannot be derived from source is labelled as needing a fixture import rather than guessed.

Exact values, never repairedPayer contributions and participant shares are checked independently and must land on the expense total. A difference is stated in the currency it was typed in, with the amount still unassigned. Nothing is distributed, absorbed or rounded on the user’s behalf. FIN-14 … FIN-20
Record and reconcile, server-confirmedTrip never moves money. A settlement is a record of a payment made elsewhere: confirmed before it is written, held while it is written, and never shown as done until the server says so. A lost confirmation resolves to the existing record, not a second one. FIN-33 … FIN-37
Two rates, two jobsThe FX tab answers what things cost today. The ledger answers what was spent, at the rate recorded with each expense. Refreshing one never restates the other, and a missing historical rate is held out for reconciliation rather than replaced with today’s. FIN-29, 42, 43, 44

EXPENSE AND SETTLEMENT REMOVAL · NOT DESIGNEDChecked before designing it: the current source has no expense or settlement delete path. Corrections are edits to the original expense (FIN-25 … FIN-28), which is also what the copy on FIN-18 tells people. Recorded settlements are permanent by design and FIN-33 says so before the write. Status: not supported in current scope — not an open design blocker.
BOARD 16 · BATCH 5 · FLOW I · MOBILE 393 × 852

Documents, scanning and reconciliation

Eighty-three screens on the existing Scan tab. The hero pair, the dashed upload target, the assignment toggle, SCAN IT, the Scanning… spinner and the previously-scanned rows are reused exactly as they are. What is added is the part a single-user build never had to answer: documents belong to one Group and are private, extraction is never authoritative, a stored object and its record can come apart, and an itinerary Event created from a scan is a different thing from the document behind it. Thirteen document states are kept distinct rather than collapsed into one spinner, and the v1 public object URL is migrated away from without ever being printed on screen.

Access is confidentiality, presentation is notA document is private to its Group: outside current same-Group authorisation there is no name, no uploader, no thumbnail, no parsed contents and no count. An Event may be presented to selected Participants, and that is placement — every active Member can read Events. The words “private Event” appear nowhere in the product. DOC-11 … DOC-18
Thirteen states, not one spinnerLocal file, uploading, private object accepted, parsing, warning, parse failure, reviewed values, Event creation, association complete, history, viewer, removal, reconciliation. Each says what exists and what does not, because “Scanning…” on its own has been quietly wrong for a decade. DOC-19 … DOC-39
Reconcilable, or heldA record without a file, a file without a record, an Event without a document, a document without its Event, and a removal that half-succeeded. Each is detected, named, and held out of use — never repaired silently, never reported as success, and never given a public fallback. DOC-61 … DOC-70

1 · DOCUMENT ACCESSWho may open the file

The document is private to the authorised Group: private from the public, private from unrelated Groups, reached only through current same-Group authorisation — never by filename, path, URL or metadata id.

CONFIDENTIALITY
2 · EVENT PRESENTATIONWho the itinerary Event is shown to

The selection decides who the extracted Event is presented to. That is placement, not secrecy: active same-Group Members retain accepted Event database-read authority.

PRESENTATION, NOT SECRECY
Said plainly in product copy: “This is a private Group document.” Never “private to the people you selected”, and never “secret Event” — neither is a promise the accepted architecture keeps.

The single most misreadable rule on this board, so it gets its own plate. There is no per-document audience: access is current same-Group authorisation, and the selection is Event presentation only. The design refuses both “private Event” and “document audience” anywhere in the product.

DOWNLOAD FAILURE · FOUR DISTINCT CAUSES
1 · CONNECTION“You’re offline. Try again when you’re back.”Retry is safe and will work later.
2 · OBJECT UNAVAILABLE“This document isn’t available right now.”Reconciliation may be needed — DOC-63.
3 · AUTHORIZATION CHANGED“This document isn’t available to you.”Same wording as DOC-55. No metadata, no reason.
4 · TRUSTED FAILURE“Something went wrong. Nothing changed.”Generic by design — and never names the service.
Four causes, four recoveries, and only three distinguishable messages — because an authorization change must read exactly like a private document to anybody who is not allowed to know the difference.

Diagnosis is for engineering; the client says only what a person can act on. Case 3 deliberately collapses into the generic unavailable wording, which is the difference between an error message and a membership oracle.

BOARD 17 · BATCH 6 · FLOW M · MOBILE 393 × 852

Group configuration and accounting currency

Eighty screens reached from the Group title in the header — no sixth tab, no admin console, no account-level trip settings. One Group owns its name, destination, dates, canonical IANA timezone, ISO 4217 accounting currency and approved display context, and only a current Owner may change any of it. The three hard parts get the most room: a timezone change that must not be described as moving Events, an accounting currency that stops being editable the moment history exists, and a display context that must never read as ledger authority.

AUTHORITYOnly a current authorised Owner may request a change. A Member reads the same values with every mutation affordance absent — a Member is not a Viewer, and the word is not used.
NEVER SILENTNo configuration change rewrites an audit fact, reinterprets a persisted instant, alters an Original amount or FX evidence, moves a record between Groups, or grants authority. Every save is server-confirmed.
THE LOCKOnce accounting history exists, ordinary editing cannot replace the accounting currency. The screen shows the lock and its cause — not a dead selector, and never a Convert everything action.
A · CONFIGURATION ENTRYReached from the Group/header menu that already switches Groups. Owner, Member, loading, denied and archived renderings of the same record.

BOARD 18 · BATCH 7 · FLOW N · MOBILE 393 × 852

Realtime, notifications and connection states

Fifty-five screens for the part of a multi-user app that is easiest to make unbearable. There is no notification centre, no bell, no inbox, no unread count and no activity feed — because none is in the accepted scope, and because a shared trip generates exactly the kind of low-value chatter those surfaces amplify. Instead there is a four-level hierarchy: silent update, temporary feedback, persistent inline notice, and conflict requiring action. Realtime is presentation only; authorisation stays on the server, updates stay Group-scoped, and nothing renders before the current reader is authorised to see it.

FOUR LEVELSLevel 1 silent update · Level 2 temporary toast or pill · Level 3 persistent inline card · Level 4 conflict card with actions. A change is assigned the lowest level that is honest.
NEVER FROM THE CHANNELNo control, row, count or value is granted by a realtime message alone. Authority comes from a confirmed authorised read; the stream only says something is worth re-reading.
NO FOCUS THEFTBackground updates never move focus, never scroll, and never reorder under a reading finger. Polite announcements for updates, assertive only when the person must act now.
A · CONNECTION LIFECYCLEHealth is silence. Every other connection state names itself once, under the header, and never blocks what is already safe to read.

BOARD 20 · BATCH 8 · FLOW P · MOBILE 393 × 852

Migration, recovery and implementation-readiness

Ninety screens for the batch nobody wants to design and everybody needs. The existing Bali trip has to become an account-owned Group without losing an Event, a rupiah or a receipt, and the person holding the phone has to be told the truth at every step — including the steps where the truth is “we stopped, and nothing changed”. Six outcomes are kept distinct and never blurred into “done”: nothing changed, change committed, rolled back, still running, outcome unknown, review required. Product copy stays in product language throughout; the identifiers a reviewer needs live in the manifests, never on a screen.

NEVER GUESSNo value is inferred to make a migration complete. A mismatch is held and named, and validation that cannot resolve something stops the release rather than choosing for it.
NEVER PARTIALA Group is fully protected or it is not available. Partial security activation and unproven cross-Group isolation both block release, and ordinary users see maintenance rather than an exposed Group.
NEVER INTERNALNo table, schema, policy, bucket, object id or stage identifier appears in any user-facing string on this board. MIG-90 draws the boundary explicitly.
A · PRE-MIGRATION COMMUNICATIONBanners, never modals. A read-only window that never reads as a locked account, and a cancellation that states plainly whether anything changed.
MIGRATION SCHEDULED
🛠This trip is being upgraded on 2 August.
TRIPBakchodi in Bali
WINDOW2 Aug, 02:00 – 04:00 WITA
DURING THAT TIMEReading works, changes don’t
EXACT FINISHNot promised
Nothing you have added is going anywhere. This is about how the trip is stored, not what is in it.
MIG-01Migration scheduled

Names the Group, the window and what stops working — and refuses to promise a finish time nobody supplied. The three read lines are the whole message; everything else on the trip stays where it is.

BOARD 21 · BATCH 1 SLICE

Interaction contracts

NAVIGATION AND BACK Authentication and onboarding are pages, not sheets: they are the whole task and browser back must be able to leave them. Once a Group is open, everything short-lived is a sheet, as it is today. Back from AUTH-01 exits. Back from ONB-03 with typed input asks “Leave without creating this Group?”. Back from ONB-05 is disabled. Back from ONB-06 does not return to the form — the Group already exists. Browser back and the header arrow do the same thing on every screen. Invitation and reset links are deep links: opening one signed out routes through AUTH-01 or AUTH-02 and returns to the link's destination afterwards.
SHEETS, ESCAPE AND FOCUS Sheets keep the current Modal geometry: overlay rgba(15,11,8,.82), blur 14px, 480px cap, 20px radius, 22px padding, slide-up entry, scroll inside the overlay. Backdrop click and Escape close any sheet with no unsaved input, and ask first when there is some. The one exception is AUTH-08, which cannot be dismissed. Opening a sheet moves focus to its heading, traps Tab inside it, and returns focus to the opening control on close. Confirmation dialogs focus the cancel action first, never the destructive one.
SERVER-CONFIRMED VERSUS OPTIMISTIC Server-confirmed, never optimistic: sign in, sign up, password reset, Group creation, invitation acceptance, ownership transfer, member removal, participant claiming, settlement recording, and any destructive Group action. The result appears only after the server says so; until then the control shows progress and the destination is not revealed. Optimistic is allowed only where it already is: toggling a todo, expanding notes, switching timezone, choosing a currency segment. Every failed action states whether anything changed. “Nothing was created” is part of the copy, not an implication.
KEYBOARD, TARGETS AND MOTION Enter submits any single-purpose form. Tab order follows visual order. Focus is always visible: accent border plus a 3px soft accent ring on fields, a 2px light outline offset 2px on pills and rows. Minimum target 44×44 everywhere, including the header chips, the Copy control, close buttons and remove crosses. Row-shaped controls use a 56px row instead. Under reduced motion: pulse and spin become a static dimmed state, slide-up and fade become instant, and progress is communicated in words instead of movement.

Interaction contracts — finance and settlement

EXACT-TOTAL VALIDATIONPayer contributions and participant shares are validated independently and continuously as values change — the one case where per-keystroke feedback is correct, because it is arithmetic rather than a verdict. Save is disabled until both totals land on the expense total within the 1 IDR tolerance the source already allows. The difference is always stated in the currency the amounts were typed in, and never redistributed.
SERVER-CONFIRMED FINANCEExpense insert, expense update, and settlement recording are all server-confirmed. The sheet holds, its fields go inert, backdrop and Escape are suspended, sibling actions are disabled so a second submission is impossible, and no row, balance, pool figure or group total moves until the server answers. Nothing is ever shown as done before that.
STALE FINANCE FORMIf authorisation or the underlying record changes while a form is open, the write is allowed to reach the server and fail there. Typed values stay visible and copyable, the screen states that nothing was saved and that balances are unchanged, and Close returns to an authorised destination. FIN-24 and FIN-28.
NO SILENT REPAIRNo rounding correction, no distributing a remainder across participants, no adjusting the last person, and no recomputing a historical value to make a total balance. Where a value cannot be reconstructed the row is held out of the totals and the total is stated as a floor until controlled reconciliation. FIN-44.
ACCOUNTING FX VERSUS LIVE FXEvery accounting figure derives from the rate recorded with its own record. The FX tab is a live estimate and refreshing it recalculates nothing on the ledger. No screen offers to restate history at today’s rate, and no rate is editable outside an accepted reconciliation operation. FIN-29, FIN-42, FIN-43.
IDEMPOTENT SETTLEMENT RETRYA retry after a lost confirmation resolves to the existing settlement and says so plainly. No duplicate row, no second balance change, and no fresh success treatment — the copy explains why the screen appeared. FIN-37.
GROUP FINANCE CONTEXT SWITCHSwitching Groups clears balances, expenses and settlement history in the same paint as the switch, then loads the new ledger behind a skeleton. There is no frame in which one Group’s figures appear under another’s heading. A failed switch leaves the previous Group selected and internally consistent; a refused switch resolves to PERM-03 with nothing behind it. FIN-45, FIN-46, FIN-47.
UNSAVED FINANCE FORMSClosing a form with typed values asks first. Discard is explicit, and the confirmation names what will be lost rather than asking a generic question.
DESTRUCTIVE AND IRREVERSIBLESettlement recording is confirmed before it is written because it cannot be removed. Expense and settlement deletion do not exist in current scope, so no destructive finance confirmation other than settlement recording is designed.
NO CLIENT-SIDE SECURITYAbsent buttons are not the enforcement. Every finance mutation is refused server-side regardless of what the client renders, and no permission state exposes which rule refused it.
BOARD 21 · CONTINUED · BATCH 3

Interaction contracts — permission and access

KNOWN AT RENDERIf the app already knows the action would be refused, no enabled control is drawn. Owner-only configuration stays visible but closed with one explanation (PERM-06); irrelevant or destructive actions are absent rather than dimmed; no form opens that cannot be submitted.
STALE DURING ACTIONIf access changes after the screen opened, the write is allowed to reach the server and fail there. Input is preserved locally and copyable, the screen states that nothing changed, the authorised view refreshes, and no success is shown before confirmation (PERM-13, 17, 18).
SERVER-CONFIRMEDInvitation acceptance, ownership transfer, member removal, participant claiming, settlement recording, archive and restore, and sensitive configuration are never optimistic. A refusal shows the unchanged state, not a rollback animation.
AUTHORISED BACKBrowser Back and the close button resolve to the nearest destination the user is still entitled to — their own Group, or the Group picker. Back never returns to a Group that just refused, and never re-fires the refused action.
NO CONTENT BEHINDA permission page replaces content; it is not an overlay over it. Nothing inaccessible remains in the DOM behind a scrim, and the paint that shows the explanation is the paint that removes the data.
ESCAPE AND BACKDROPPermission sheets dismiss on Escape and on backdrop tap, because dismissing changes nothing. Confirmation sheets that would mutate keep backdrop-dismiss but return focus to the trigger.
FOCUSA server-denied form moves focus to the summary and announces it politely; the summary is the labelled description of the disabled Save. Closing a sheet restores focus to the control that opened it.
PRIVACY-SAFE HANDLINGEvents outside a participant’s presentation are omitted — no locked placeholder, no ghost row, no effect on any count or total. Documents are not presentation-filtered; they are private to the Group. A stale direct reference yields one generic unavailable state with no metadata and no indication that the resource exists.
SESSION VERSUS ACCESSExpiry routes to authentication with a continuation; denial leaves the session untouched. No permission screen contains a sign-in control (PERM-19).
RETRYTry again appears only where retrying can change the answer — connection and storage. Permission, expiry, revocation and conflict states offer a different action or none, and say why.
TOUCH AND MOTIONEvery control on these screens is at least 44×44 with 56px rows; reduced-motion removes sheet slide and spinner rotation, keeping a static mono status.

Interaction contracts — documents and scanning

Fourteen contracts for board 16. Nothing here is optimistic: object acceptance, parsing, Event creation, presentation changes, removal and reconciliation are all server-confirmed, and each one states what exists after it fails.

File selection and replacementTapping the target opens the platform chooser; the application owns everything before and after it (DOC-10). Replace sits beside Remove so a wrong pick costs one tap. Cancellation leaves the previous selection exactly as it was, and a lost file handle clears the selection rather than keeping a dead reference. DOC-04, DOC-05, DOC-09, DOC-10
Unsaved review-form handlingReviewed values survive a failed Event creation and are offered back verbatim (DOC-37). They are not offered back after a permission denial, because there is nowhere valid to submit them (DOC-38). Discard is explicit; nothing auto-saves a half-reviewed booking as an Event. DOC-26, DOC-30, DOC-37, DOC-38
Backdrop, Escape and focusSheets and the document viewer trap focus, close on Escape and on backdrop tap, and return focus to the row or control that opened them. Destructive confirmations never focus the destructive action by default. The viewer is a sheet, not a browser tab, so Escape is always available. DOC-49 … DOC-51, DOC-57, CMP-44, CMP-45
Progress announcementsUpload percentage, storage acceptance, parsing and Event creation announce politely and once per state change — never per frame. Under reduced motion the progress bar becomes a static fill and every spinner becomes a static indicator; no state depends on movement to be understood. DOC-19 … DOC-22, DOC-35, E-04, E-05
Parser warning navigationWarnings sit on their own fields with their own reasons, and a focusable summary strip moves focus to the first one. Caution styling is used only where user review can resolve the problem; anything that blocks creation is an error on the field it belongs to. DOC-27, DOC-31, DOC-32, CMP-39
Server-confirmed Event creationThe Create action is replaced by a progress state rather than disabled, so duplicate submission is impossible by construction. No Event appears in the itinerary until the server confirms it, and no partial Event is ever displayed after a failure. DOC-35, DOC-36, DOC-37
Safe retry boundariesRetry is offered where it can succeed and declared safe where it cannot duplicate: before object acceptance nothing was stored (DOC-23), a failed parse leaves a stored document (DOC-24), a failed Event write leaves no Event (DOC-37). Retry is not offered after a denial or after a detected inconsistency. DOC-23, DOC-24, DOC-37, DOC-61
Duplicate submission preventionOne in-flight operation per document at a time. Upload disables assignment and Replace; parsing disables everything but Stop; creation replaces its own button; removal disables itself and does not hide the row ahead of the server. DOC-19, DOC-21, DOC-35, DOC-58
Document removal confirmationDeliberate confirmation with the impact enumerated, never a bare are-you-sure. It states that the document goes, the Event stays with its provenance, and access ends for everyone. The destructive action is not the default focus. DOC-57, CMP-45, E-02, E-14
Group-switch clearing behaviourClear, then load, then render — in that order, always. The old Group’s documents leave the client before the new request is made, so no merged list can exist even briefly and a denial has nothing behind it to reveal. DOC-76, DOC-77, DOC-78
Stale presentation handlingA participant who has left is removed from the selection in place, with the file, the remaining assignment and the flow position preserved. No write is attempted against a membership list the client knows is out of date. DOC-17, DOC-18, PERM-17
Reconciliation status handlingVerification changes nothing and widens no access. Success restores consistency without granting privilege; failure states that no exposure occurred and no Event was fabricated. Ordinary Members get plain guidance and no repair controls. DOC-67 … DOC-70, CMP-46
Document access versus Event presentationTwo separate guarantees, rendered as two separate statements wherever both apply. Document access is confidentiality. Event presentation is placement, and every active Member can read Events. The phrase private Event is prohibited in product copy. DOC-13, DOC-16, DOC-34, CMP-41
Private viewer and download behaviourAuthorization is checked before any content is fetched, so nothing paints early. Rendering happens in-app from a short-lived authorised read: no address bar, no copyable link, no permanent URL, and a download is a transfer rather than a link handout. DOC-49 … DOC-53, CMP-44, E-15
BOARD 21 · CONTINUED · BATCH 6

Interaction contracts — Group configuration

Fifteen contracts for board 17. Every one of them is a promise about what does not move: identity, membership, recorded instants, Original amounts, FX evidence and settled history are outside the reach of every screen on that board.

Group settings entry and BackOpened from the Group title in the header, never from a tab. Browser Back returns to the prior authorised Group screen; an unavailable Group routes to safe Group selection rather than leaving settings behind an overlay.
Owner versus Member renderingIdentical rows, identical heights, identical values. Owner rows carry Edit; Member rows carry nothing at all. No dimmed control, and the word Viewer is never used for a Member.
Field validation timingOn submit, not on keystroke. Each field validates independently, so one invalid row never invalidates a valid one, and every error is rendered against its own field.
Server-confirmed saveNo header, date line, Event rendering or currency label updates before the server confirms. Cancel is unavailable in flight and the sheet cannot be dismissed mid-write.
Stale-version handlingA changed Group version rejects the write. Reload current configuration, copy unsaved text, cancel — three choices and no auto-merge, matching PERM-17 and PERM-18.
Unsaved-change confirmationThe accepted confirmation-sheet geometry. Discard carries the destructive tint because it loses work; leaving does not.
Focus entry and returnFocus enters the first editable field on open and returns to the row that launched the editor on close or cancel. Escape closes and returns focus without saving.
Configuration refresh after successThe current Group context refreshes once, after confirmation, and every dependent surface lands in the same frame. No staggered updates.
Group-switch clearingOld configuration clears, loading holds the geometry, and the new name, dates, timezone and accounting currency appear together. No frame renders mixed Group configuration.
Archived-state handlingArchive-aware reads keep values legible; every mutation control is absent. An Owner keeps Restore. A save that loses the race to an archive is refused and routed.
Accounting-currency lockLocked once accounting history exists. The lock is shown with its cause, never as a disabled selector, and no in-app conversion action exists on any screen.
Timezone impact confirmationConfirmation states that existing instants are unchanged and their displayed local time may change. It never claims Events are shifted, and audit facts are never rewritten.
Display context versus ledger authorityDisplay currencies are reference context. The accounting currency cannot be removed from required accounting presentation, and refreshing FX cannot change a balance.
Reduced-motion alternativesThe saving spinner becomes a static state label under prefers-reduced-motion; the realtime banner appears without transition; skeletons hold geometry without pulsing.
Screen-reader announcementsErrors announce politely against their field. Save results announce once, assertively, and name the outcome: settings updated, or nothing was changed. The lock notice is read as text, not as a disabled control.
BOARD 21 · CONTINUED · BATCH 7

Interaction contracts — realtime and connection

Sixteen contracts for board 18. The through-line is that a realtime message is never authority: it says something is worth re-reading, and everything a person is then allowed to see or do comes from a confirmed authorised read.

Four-level hierarchyA change is assigned the lowest honest level: silent update, temporary toast or pill, persistent inline card, or conflict card with actions. Level 4 is the only level with buttons.
Group-scoped subscription lifecycleSubscribe on entering a Group, unsubscribe on leaving it, and never hold two Group subscriptions at once. Cross-Group payloads are not filtered client-side; they are not received.
Authorisation before renderNothing renders from a payload alone. The client re-reads authorised data and renders that, so the channel can never become a side door around Group authorisation.
Old Group unsubscribe and clearingRT-10 fixes the order: unsubscribe, clear, resolve membership, subscribe, fetch, render. Steps two and five are what make a mixed-Group frame impossible rather than unlikely.
DeduplicationPresentation is idempotent by accepted record identity, not by timing. A duplicate arriving a minute later is still a duplicate and changes nothing on screen.
Idempotent local echoYour own settlement returns to you through the channel. Local result and echo describe one accepted record, so one success and one history row are shown.
Complete dependent-state refreshA finance mutation fans out to totals, balances and suggested transfers. All of them repaint together or none do; partially updated money is never rendered.
Stale form handlingIf a form is open, the update becomes a conflict card. Local input is preserved, nothing is merged, and the eventual save still goes through server-confirmed stale-version protection.
Out-of-order eventsA known older revision is never painted over a newer accepted state. Where ordering cannot be established the client refreshes instead of guessing.
Scroll and focus preservationBackground updates never move focus, never scroll and never reorder under a reading finger. New rows append; they do not insert above the reading position.
Status announcementsPolite for background updates, assertive only when the person must act now. Every essential outcome also lands in durable screen state, never only in a toast.
Reduced motionThe reconnecting pulse becomes a static dot, toasts appear without transition, and skeletons hold geometry without animating.
Offline versus realtime-only failureOffline stops reads and writes; a realtime-only failure stops neither. RT-05 and RT-08 are deliberately different screens because the available actions differ.
Session expiry distinctionA session expiry is about the person; a permission change is about the Group. RT-50 keeps four causes separate because each routes somewhere different.
Membership removal responseClear content, unsubscribe, route, then explain. The order is the contract: no inaccessible content ever waits behind a dialog.
Archived-state responseMutation affordances are removed the moment archival is confirmed, so nobody starts an action the server has already begun refusing.
BOARD 21 · CONTINUED · BATCH 8

Interaction contracts — migration, recovery and release

Ten contracts for board 20. Every one of them is a rule about what the product is allowed to claim, because in a migration the copy is the only thing most people will ever see of the operation.

Maintenance navigationA cold start during the window routes to the migration state, never a generic server error. The tab bar stays; the app is unavailable, not broken.
Read-only maintenanceReads continue across Events, finance, documents and todos. Mutation controls are absent rather than disabled, and the copy always states that the account is fine.
Unsaved work at cutoverLocal text is preserved and offered back. The screen states that nothing was saved before it offers anything else.
Never guess a valueValidation that cannot resolve something stops the migration. No default is selected, no balance is repaired and no participant is matched automatically.
Six distinct outcomesNothing changed, change committed, rolled back, still running, outcome unknown, review required. The weakest badge the evidence supports is the one that is used.
Rollback is not successA running rollback is reported as running. MIG-36 uses the sanctioned sentence — the previous Trip data is still in place — and claims nothing beyond it.
Recovery grants nothingVerification phases create nothing, delete nothing and widen no access. A repair that quietly widened access would be a privacy regression dressed as a fix.
No self-service retry where retry cannot workA Retry button that cannot succeed is worse than none. MIG-32 and MIG-38 offer waiting and controlled support instead.
Release gatePartial security activation and unproven cross-Group isolation both block release. There is no degraded middle setting and no exception path.
Product language onlyNo table, schema, policy, bucket, object id or stage identifier appears in a user-facing string. MIG-90 draws the boundary and the manifests hold the internal side of it.
BOARD 22 + 23 · CONTINUED · BATCHES 7 AND 8

Accessibility corrections — realtime, migration and export evidence

Additions to the accessibility board for the two new batches, plus the export-template correction that affects every annotated file in the package.

Realtime announcementsBackground updates announce politely and never move focus. Assertive announcements are reserved for changes that stop the person acting — access removed, form no longer saveable.
No focus theftA list that grows under a typing finger is the fastest way to lose a caret. New rows append below the reading position and the caret is never relocated by a remote change.
Toast timingTemporary feedback stays long enough to be perceived and read, and every outcome it carries is also present in durable screen state for anyone who missed it.
Migration progress semanticsProgress steps are a list with per-step status text, not a bare spinner. Done, current and pending differ in fill and weight as well as colour.
Long-running statusNo indefinite animation without status copy. A silent spinner is indistinguishable from a hang for every user and impossible for a screen-reader user.
Maintenance read-only semanticsAbsent controls rather than disabled ones, so assistive technology reports a smaller surface rather than a wall of unavailable buttons.
Colour is never the only signalTruth-state badges, connection pills and claim states all carry a word as well as a hue. MIG-89 is readable in greyscale.
Corrected annotation templateAnnotation cards now stack the Screen ID above a full-width title, so a title that re-measures wider in the export renderer grows the card instead of overprinting the paragraph. Every annotated PNG in the package was regenerated from the corrected template.

STILL TO DESIGN · BATCHES 4–8
Board 20 tablet and desktop reference frames remain documented inside boards 04 and 20 rather than as separate image exports. Batches 5 to 8 extend boards 19 and 21 to 24 rather than restating them. Board numbering follows the order the batches arrive, so finance is board 15.
RESOLVED DECISIONS · APPLIED TO THIS PACKAGE
O-01 Roles — resolved. Exactly Owner and Member. Viewer and every additional role are deferred. Read-only presentation survives for archived Groups, denied actions, stale state and maintenance, but it is not a role. O-02 Group configuration — resolved. Name, destination, start date, end date, canonical IANA timezone, accounting currency and approved currency-display context all belong to the Group, set at creation and editable in configuration. O-03 Link lifetimes — resolved. Group invitations expire after 7 days and are single-use. Verification and reset link durations are provider configuration and are never promised in copy; expired links use generic copy. O-04 Participant emoji — resolved. The five migrated Bali participants keep their animal emoji. New participants use initials. Emoji selection and automatic assignment are deferred. O-05 Group deletion — resolved. No permanent deletion in scope. Leave Group, last-Owner protection, Archive and Restore are designed on board 10. Purge, retention and anonymisation remain unresolved and undesigned. O-06 Conflicting design system — resolved. The attached green enterprise-learning system is ignored entirely. The current Trip application and the accepted UI baseline are the only visual authority.
O-07 contested claims — resolved. No Owner review queue, approval screen or manual override in scope. A claim that lacks evidence, conflicts, is already taken or cannot resolve atomically stops safely, states that nothing changed, and offers retry only where retry could succeed (PERM-16, CLM-09, CLM-11). O-08 retention and purge — resolved as deferred. No permanent deletion, purge, anonymisation, attribution removal or retention control is designed. Groups archive and restore; historical expenses, settlements, documents and recorder attribution remain; removed participants keep their historical display identity. E-10 and E-11 — approved in batch 4. Permission pages replace content and hide the tab bar when no Group resolves; dead mutation controls are removed rather than dimmed. C-07, C-09, C-10, C-13, C-14 and C-15 closed — C-10 restated: Event presentation filters may be applied before participant-specific itinerary counts and presentation summaries are rendered. That is presentation parity, not database confidentiality, and documents are not audience-filtered in the current accepted target. C-13 closes as a target security correction (private Storage, no permanent public URL, no path-based authority), C-14 as a target reconciliation correction, C-15 as a target provenance correction.
O-01 to O-18 are all resolved. O-16 Trip-name length is implementation-configured; O-17 a reviewed accounting-currency migration is outside ordinary Owner authority and has no executable workflow in this package; O-18 approved display-currency context is Group configuration and per-reader preferences are deferred. D-01 to D-04 carry final statuses: warm image fallback with no broken-image glyph, contextual realtime surfaces with no notification centre, accessibility specified with implementation verification still required, and emoji selection deferred. C-01 to C-15 are all closed. E-01 to E-16 are all decided.
Requires formal review: R-01 IR ownership and wave assignment cannot be proven from the Accepted roadmap inside this package, so every screen is marked Requires roadmap mapping rather than carrying an invented identifier · R-02 measured contrast, keyboard traversal and reduced-motion verification on a real build.
SELF-REVIEW · READINESS
✓ No unexplained visual change. Every deviation is C-, T-, M-, A-, P- or E-numbered. ✓ Five-tab shell intact; no sixth tab; AI and legacy Group Settings not treated as current. ✓ Participant colours used for identity only; role never colour-only. ✓ Every state in this batch has a frame or a component variant; none exists only as prose. ✓ Tablet and desktop behaviour shown; no new breakpoint. ✓ Placeholders are declared as open items, not hidden.
Batch 7 adds board 18: fifty-five realtime, notification and connection screens on a four-level hierarchy — silent update, temporary feedback, persistent inline notice, conflict requiring action — with ten components and no notification centre, bell, inbox, unread count or activity feed. Batch 8 adds board 20: ninety migration, recovery and implementation-readiness screens with fourteen components, six mutually exclusive data-change outcomes, and a release gate that blocks on partial security activation or unproven cross-Group isolation. O-16, O-17 and O-18 are resolved; D-01 to D-04 carry final statuses; every annotated export was regenerated from the corrected annotation template; and invented roadmap identifiers were removed package-wide. Not Accepted. Not Locked.
